- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.25) over recent days, reduce forecasted price targets; model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment (e.g., >0.5), reduce subsequent values to avoid overshoot; market often corrects after initial rally.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after recent peak), model tends to overestimate continuation — apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >5% deviation) and sentiment is neutral or positive, reduce forecast by 10–20% to align with sentiment-driven correction.  
- If sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment (e.g., >0.5 for 3+ days), model often overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or adjust downward if sentiment drops.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each day after the 10th day of the forecast window.  
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop — increase forecast downward by 2–5% to reflect sentiment-driven sell-off.
